method: Both reviewers read every German string of the unit again: title and title.canDo, spec.situation and spec.deviation, the Folge (7 lines and the gist item), the three inputs (30 lines, Elif's written reply, Sophie's postcard and Priya's chat message), the two L1 texts (71 and 68 words, recounted), the strategy card, 8 Redemittel, the Sp2 task (instructions, situation, cards, persona, openingLine, hintWords, 8 model turns), the S2 task (situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte with cues, checklist, 33-word model text), both Aussprache blocks, the three micro-outputs, the Check line, story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine, promptDe, option and explanation.de. We also read the two shared rule cards the unit shows (rc.perfekt-haben in LS1 and LS3, rc.zeitangaben-inversion in LS2) as RuleCardView renders them, i.e. under the step's modelSentence, and the 28 u11 word cards (lexicon.json examples). We solved all 88 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: 1 Folge gist, 15 input items, 12 structuredInput, 33 pool items, 12 reserve, 5 exam items, 8 check items and 2 proof items. For sentence_building we permuted the tiles; for error_correction we tried every one-word and every Mittelfeld repair. Risky answers were graded with the player's src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js: ls3-p10 „Ich habe ein Buch am Sonntag gelesen.“ → wrong; ls2-p04 „letzte Woche“ → typo, „Letzte Woche“ → correct; ls1-i03 „40 Euro“, ls2-i04 „11 Uhr“ / „elf Uhr“, ls2-i05 „17 Uhr“ → wrong; ls1-p10 „Ich habe am Freitag Fisch gegessen.“, c07 „Ein Fahrrad haben wir gekauft.“, ls1-i03 „vierzig“ → correct; q02 „gestern“ and ls3-i04 „mittwoch“ → typo. Every German string was scanned against knownForms + licensedForms + compounds + metalanguage at a1.1-u11 (lib-validate), including the surfaces the LEX-01 rail does not walk (input titles, Aussprache focus, strategy card, Redemittel labels, cliffhanger) and the u11 word-card examples. Sentence lengths of all inputs and exam texts were measured against level-profiles.json a1.1 (sentence.maxWords 12, meanWordsMax 7). The exam block and both tasks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (sd1.l1, sd1.sp2, sd1.s2) and the compiled rubrics (sd1-sp2, sd1-s2, course-micro, course-micro-sp); the writing pre-check was read in src/components/course-v2/WritingTaskView.jsx (cueFound) and the speaking partner prompt in netlify/functions/_shared/speakingAI.mjs (cards-ask). The Fact a1.1-u11-f01 was re-read at its source (skd.museum/besuch/residenzschloss/, fetched 2026-09-28). Cast and story were checked against casts/series.json, casts/a1.json and units u01, u03, u06, u09, u10 and u12; the unit against curriculum/a1-1.json u11 and registries/cando/a1.json. Every r1 finding was verified (previousFindings), and every finding class of the u04 trail (r1–r5) and of the sibling a1.1 r2 reviews (u09 r2, u10 r2) was checked for recurrence. Every fix proposed below was checked against knownForms + licensedForms and TXT-04 (≤ 90 characters) before it was recommended.

verdict: Not exit-ready, but the unit itself is close: 0 BLOCKER, 1 MAJOR (on a shared rule card, not in the unit file) and 10 MINOR, 6 of them unit-owned one- or two-line edits. The r1 fixes are real. 12 of 16 r1 findings are fixed, 2 are partly fixed, and the 2 still open belong to the lexicon and rule-cards owners. The validator exits 0 with one advisory. The postcard now exists on a possible day: it is written on Monday, read on Tuesday, and invites to the WG. Every one of the 88 keys is right, the German is correct and idiomatic on every model surface, and du/Sie is right in every relationship. L1, Sp2 and S2 match sd1.json, and the tasks are original. The story joins u09, u10 and u12, and the Dresden Fact is current (re-read at the source today). One MAJOR stops exit, and no rail catches it (F01): rc.perfekt-haben's table puts „Ich habe“, „Wir haben“ and „Was hast du“ under the header „Position 2“. RuleCardView shows this table directly under the inverted model sentences „Am Samstag habe ich …“ / „Am Abend haben wir …“, which gives the learner exactly the V3 order that r1-F05 took out of three explanations. The minors: four items the learner can solve without processing the target, one of them a side effect of our own r1-F07 fix and one of r1-F09 (F02); a marked but correct correction graded wrong (F03); a micro-output whose prompt cannot earn its target point (F04); a pre-check cue that the required Anrede always ticks (F05); a 14-word postcard sentence with „bis in die Nacht“, created by the r1 LEX-02 fix (F06); three misquoted explanations (F07). Owner-held: r1-F14(b)(c) (F08), three u11 word cards that reopen r1 classes (F09), r1-F16 (F10), and the checker's number-plus-unit-word class from u10 r2 (F11).

scoreNotes.D: No error and no unidiomatic phrase on any model surface after r1-F08. du/Sie fits every relationship: Frau Schulz uses Sie with surnames, the friends and the chat use du, and Nora and every task use Sie. The explanation misquotes (F07) are scored under A.
scoreNotes.N: The rule card that carries the unit's new grammar mislabels the positions and so teaches V3 (F01, MAJOR). Also: one input sentence is over the A1.1 maximum length and contains an unlicensed „bis in die Nacht“ (F06); receptive lemmas are produced and Sonntag is mis-allocated (F08); three word cards reopen r1 classes (F09); the LS2 card does not show the step's past time words (F10). Coverage and the grammar ceiling are clean on every unit surface.
scoreNotes.H: The scenes are lively and believable: Olena's 40-euro bike and „Ich bekomme nie Postkarten!“, Bilal asleep in the cinema, the delayed train and the coffee, Emre in İzmir seeing the photos in the course chat. All four can-dos are performed: narrating in LS1 and Sp2, time words in LS2, q02 and Sp2, reading the postcard and the chat in LS3 and L1, and the post in S2. The postcard scene now works.
scoreNotes.A: No wrong key, no ambiguous item, and the explanations now name the real position. It is 4, not 5, because four items do no work on their target (F02), one marked but correct repair is graded wrong (F03), one micro-output prompt cannot earn its target point (F04), and three explanations misquote the speakers (F07).
scoreNotes.P: L1 is exact: 2 texts of 71 and 68 words in [56, 92], 5 R/F items, 2 R / 3 F with no run, original. Sp2 is exact: 2 topics, one card each per candidate, question then answer, prep 0, rubric sd1-sp2. It is a single-Teil task, so the multi-Teil engine blocker of u01/u09/u10 r2-F01 does not apply; speakingAI's cards-ask rule reads task.cards. S2 has 3 Leitpunkte, Anrede and Gruß outside them, and 25–35 words, and its deviation from the SD1 purpose types is logged by plan decision, hence 4.
scoreNotes.K: Cast and timeline agree with u09, u10 and u12 (Friday party at the Restaurant Kochi; Saturday in Dresden; the 60-minute delay; Sophie back on Wednesday; Herr Richter and the A1.2 enrolment resolved in u12). The Fact is current. It is 4 because one word card contradicts the unit's central fact („Vorgestern war Sophie in Leipzig.“, F09).
scoreNotes.E: Each LS fits its 20 minutes at A1.1, all instructions are ≤ 90 characters, and the end screens name the win in known words. The S2 pre-check tells every learner who writes the required Anrede that the „mit wem“ point is there (F05).

findings.problem: The r1-F02 fix corrected the card's text but not its table. The table has no Position-1 column, and its header „Position 2“ stands over „Ich habe“, „Wir haben“ and „Was hast du“. This is the r1-F05 class (subject plus verb described as position 2), now on the rule card, where the r1 fix to three explanations did not reach. RuleCardView prints the step's model sentence directly above the table, and both are inverted: „Am Samstag“ and „Am Abend“ are on position 1. A learner who puts the two together („Am Samstag“, then Position 2 „ich habe“) builds ✗„Am Samstag ich habe Fußball gespielt“. That is the V3 error which ls2-p10, ls2-r03 and ls1-r04 correct. The table also contradicts the card's own sentence („haben auf Position 2“) and rc.zeitangaben-inversion, which the learner saw in u07 and sees again in LS2 (Position 0 | Position 1 | Position 2). Every other position table in the a1.1 cards (rc.verbposition-2, rc.trennbare-verben, rc.koennen, rc.zeitangaben-inversion) has separate Position-1 and Position-2 columns. GRM-05 checks word count, model sentence and twin, and the ITM-11 proposal of r1-F05 reads only explanation.de, so the class passes every rail. That is a gate hole, hence MAJOR.
findings.fix: Rule-cards owner: replace the table with [[„Position 1“, „Position 2“, „…“, „Ende: Partizip“], [„Ich“, „habe“, „am Samstag Pizza“, „gemacht.“], [„Am Samstag“, „habe“, „ich Pizza“, „gemacht.“], [„Was“, „hast“, „du gestern“, „gegessen?“], [„Gestern“, „war“, „ich in Dresden.“, „–“]]. The second row mirrors the card's own model sentence. The last row shows the war/hatte chunk that the r1-F02 text added, in the same frame and without a participle. The text stays at 59 words, and every token of the new rows is known at a1.1-u11 (knownForms + licensedForms; Position and Partizip are metalanguage).
findings.proposedRule: GRM-05: in a rule-card table whose header row names positions, a „Position N“ column (N ≥ 2) must have a „Position N−1“ column to its left, and no body cell under „Position N“ may begin with a subject pronoun or name followed by a finite verb. Failing fixture: rc.perfekt-haben (a1.1). The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.problem: The u04 r1-F26 / r2-F03 class returns in four items: the key can be reached without processing the target form. Three of them are in the Structured-Input slot, whose job is to make the form carry the meaning. (1) The r1-F07 fix removed the shared string from ls1-s02, but the two distractors now mean the same thing (jetzt is part of heute). Only one option can be right, so both „Ja“ options fall out together, and the key is the only „Nein“. The item is solved by elimination, without reading habe … gekocht as past. (2) ls1-s03 asks where „gesehen“ stands in a five-word sentence that is on the screen, and the answer is visible. (3) The key of ls3-s03 follows from the meaning of lachen, which the English prompt supplies, and the tense plays no role: the item works the same with „Wir lachen viel.“ (4) The r1-F09 fix, which we proposed, put the answer into the cue of ls2-p04. findings.proposedRule: ITM-01 advisory: (a) a fill_blank whose bracketed cue equals its key after case-folding is reported; (b) a structured-input choice item whose distractors all carry one polarity („Ja …“) and whose key carries the other („Nein …“) is reported. Failing fixtures: a1.1-u11 ls2-p04 and ls1-s02. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.problem: checkItem grades „Ich habe ein Buch am Sonntag gelesen.“ WRONG. The item's task is the sentence bracket (errorTag satzklammer), and this answer closes it. Object before the time phrase in the Mittelfeld is grammatical, with the stress on „am Sonntag“. It is no more marked than the fronted object „Ein Buch habe ich am Sonntag gelesen.“, which the item accepts. Accepting the rarer order and rejecting this one is the shape of u04 r2-F02 (minor). findings.fix: Add „Ich habe ein Buch am Sonntag gelesen.“ to accepted, with acceptedWhy „grammatisch, aber betont: „am Sonntag“ ist wichtig; die Satzklammer „habe … gelesen“ ist richtig“.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-09: an error_correction item tagged satzklammer or v2-inv is checked like sentence_building. Every V2 order that orders.mjs accepts for the constituents of its key must be in accepted[]. Failing fixture: a1.1-u11 ls3-p10. The test runs over all registered courses.
